quote: At Jerusalem he founded a city in place of the one which had been razed to the ground, naming it Aelia Capitolina
summary: Dio gives the founding of Aelia Capitolina, with a temple of Jupiter on the Temple site, as the cause of a war 'of no slight importance nor of brief duration', and says the Jews sabotaged weapons they were ordered to make.
limits: Dio is a Roman senator writing about a century after the war and the text is an 11th-century epitome. The Historia Augusta gives a different cause (circumcision ban); see the separate candidates. Dating of the colony's foundation relative to the revolt is itself debated.

quote: Soon, however, all Judaea had been stirred up, and the Jews everywhere were showing signs of disturbance
summary: Dio says unrest reached 'the Jews everywhere' and that many outside nations joined 'through eagerness for gain'; Hadrian sent his best generals, first Julius Severus from Britain.
limits: Single narrative source; 'the whole earth ... stirred up' is rhetoric and no diaspora rising in 132-135 is documented by Dio. Eck (JRS 1999) and the Current Epigraphy report cite Roman diplomas and inscriptions as showing the army effort was real, but they do not show a diaspora revolt.

limits: Posen preview is partial (rest behind free registration) and the Greek tile is from IJO 3.86 per Posen; I did not open Kraeling 1956. Dura fell c. 256-257, so the synagogue is a Roman-Parthian frontier diaspora community, not evidence about Judaea.

quote: Above all it has been maintained that the threat to Roman power constituted by the revolt has been grossly exaggerated.
summary: Eck's opening extract says the scholarly debate over the revolt's causes, course and result has not reached unanimity and counters the view that Rome's reaction proves nothing, citing 'powerful evidence which comes from Rome itself'.
limits: Only the open Cambridge extract was read, not the argument. It addresses the Roman scale of the war, not diaspora effects. A report of Eck's 2008 lecture (currentepigraphy.org, opened) says diplomas show recruiting of 2600-5300 fleet men in 134, supporting Dio's 'whole earth stirred up'.
